Distro advisory fixture provenance (acquired 2026-10-09)
=======================================================

All JSON fixtures are byte-for-byte HTTPS responses from the OSV API, which
retains each vendor's source URL in database_specific.source. They have not been
rewritten to match lindm. OSV is a transport/normalization source, not evidence
that every distro publishes complete binary-package mappings. These fixtures do
not imply complete ecosystem coverage. No network access is required by tests.

ubuntu-USN-6859-1.json (3242 bytes)
  GET https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/USN-6859-1
  SHA256 e179d515688434574c1835bbff757f0839e37e08fd8d3301168513cbcbdd2f4e
  Vendor https://github.com/canonical/ubuntu-security-notices/blob/main/osv/usn/USN-6859-1.json
  Advisory https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-6859-1
  Copyright Canonical Ltd and contributors. CC-BY-SA-4.0:
  https://github.com/canonical/ubuntu-security-notices/blob/main/LICENSE
  https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode
  Original response includes both jammy and noble; tests require noble only.
  Noble source openssh and explicit binary maps fix 1:9.6p1-3ubuntu13.3.
  No binary-to-source map is invented when that upstream information is absent.

debian-DSA-5724-1.json (578 bytes)
  GET https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/DSA-5724-1
  SHA256 26841e28408b0912ae777691790b8e966492d9b6fc92c42aa3eab648a92b7e58
  Vendor https://storage.googleapis.com/debian-osv/dsa-osv/DSA-5724-1.json
  Upstream https://www.debian.org/security/2024/dsa-5724
  Debian Security Team; source-only openssh, Debian 12, fix 1:9.2p1-2+deb12u3.
  Licensing caveat: no explicit blanket data license was located for the tracker
  export; GPL notices on tracker software must not be represented as a license
  for all vulnerability data. This tiny original factual regression specimen is
  retained with attribution. Resolve data redistribution terms with the Debian
  Security Team before public redistribution of the fixture/database:
  https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/
  https://lists.debian.org/debian-security-tracker/2026/09/msg00023.html

rocky-RLSA-2024-6783.json (1308 bytes)
  GET https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/RLSA-2024%3A6783
  SHA256 2be38769894ce8b419202930dd5fbdd1e2c64db48ae3f6de7e9d2c39f5e524db
  Vendor https://storage.googleapis.com/resf-osv-data/RLSA-2024:6783.json
  Advisory https://errata.rockylinux.org/RLSA-2024:6783
  Credits Rocky Enterprise Software Foundation and Red Hat. Vendor attributes
  Red Hat RHSA-2024:6783 under CC-BY-4.0, with vendor modifications:
  https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
  No local modifications. OSV names openssl only, although the vendor HTML lists
  openssl-libs/devel/perl too. Therefore Rocky OSV imports NEVER establish complete
  binary coverage; no absent binary map is inferred from an SRPM-looking name.
  Fix 1:3.0.7-28.el9_4 is a distro backport, not upstream OpenSSL's release fix.

fedora44-repomd.xml (7055 bytes)
  GET https://dl.fedoraproject.org/pub/fedora/linux/updates/44/Everything/x86_64/repodata/repomd.xml
  SHA256 1660dfbeda6955b4677a244cfc7af321e4ed5bb6e1aff2eac11bdfb32e2564ee
  Original repomd response; references this exact immutable updateinfo object:
  https://dl.fedoraproject.org/pub/fedora/linux/updates/44/Everything/x86_64/repodata/f7508933e5ed78ccc41d1cea6dc7d5f93d998b7fe97e7c9e84268e2ce8aadcac-updateinfo.xml.zst
  Original compressed bytes: 2176421
  Compressed SHA256 f7508933e5ed78ccc41d1cea6dc7d5f93d998b7fe97e7c9e84268e2ce8aadcac
  Decompressed bytes: 46007906
  Decompressed SHA256 d29325ac2ed7bd60d9553d834a6ae6d1675e5e2f9d0be6572ada182d1110f52d
  The entire object was actually downloaded and decompressed with zstd, not
  manufactured from a Bodhi API example. To keep the fixture small, the full
  compressed/decompressed objects are not checked in. Metadata research found
  3105 entries: 409 security, 907 bugfix, 979 enhancement, 151 newpackage, 659
  unspecified. One explicitly labelled Fedora45 nonsecurity shim entry occurs
  in this Fedora44 repository; product-labelled records must not be mixed.

fedora44-sudo.xml (14113 bytes)
  Exact contiguous <update ...>...</update> bytes extracted from that original
  XML for FEDORA-2026-7d4732cbab; not parsed/reserialized, values not changed,
  no fabricated collection/root added, no trailing newline added.
  SHA256 3ed801b9bccd9f65bbba7d04421fb0395549cd4f076699fedc5f1d7915476d0f
  Advisory https://bodhi.fedoraproject.org/updates/FEDORA-2026-7d4732cbab
  Vendor fixed binaries: 0:1.9.17-10.p2.fc44 (CVE-2026-96512 in description).
  Exact CVE tokens explicitly disclosed in vendor description/summary are
  retained even when structured references are empty; no package-name inference.
  Tests bind x86_64/noarch records; source and foreign architectures cannot leak.
  Copyright (C) 2026 Red Hat, Inc. and others, retained in the original node.
  Fedora content default CC-BY-SA-4.0, subject to explicit upstream licenses:
  https://docs.fedoraproject.org/en-US/legal/fpca/
  https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode
  Extraction is the only local change. A single update is partial coverage.
  Synthetic transport/compression envelopes in tests are labelled as such and
  do not pretend to be a complete downloaded vendor snapshot.
  The console demo (devlab.ConfigureConsoleDemo) serves this node inside a
  synthetic <updates> root as the complete updateinfo of its fixture-owned
  controlled repository: complete coverage of that demo repository, never of
  the Fedora 44 updates repository.

fedora45-shim.xml (1877 bytes)
  Exact contiguous original node for FEDORA-2026-47312bda9b from the same
  downloaded Fedora44 updateinfo object; it explicitly names Fedora45/F45.
  SHA256 f4a4a9f276aed0e061a2aabe3c4fbee06f2630eb4a105f426128d4c60f230928
  Copyright (C) 2026 Red Hat, Inc. and others; Fedora licensing links above.
  Extraction only, no rewritten product labels. The regression combines this
  original node with the original sudo node in an explicitly synthetic XML
  wrapper and requires that Fedora45 never enter Fedora44 findings.

Native version vectors
----------------------

dpkg-versions.txt: all 43 original __DATA__ rows, unchanged, from:
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guillemj/dpkg/f4941036b04e787c2803d6359802d6725d2476c6/scripts/t/Dpkg_Version.t
  Original source SHA256 59c8d762acef6cb718dc9b755c04fb070a4ad9e691b57bc0e479e3f188ca36ae
  Extracted rows SHA256 41d0adf1fe8ee5215754547a9f52b279cafbdc06a7be11aa40e573f12f8874e2
  Upstream test file declares GPL-2.0-or-later and no warranty. Only input/result
  data are retained here, not upstream Perl implementation/test machinery.
  https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html

rpm-versions.txt: all 91 active RPMVERCMP(a, b, result) rows, with only the
  macro wrapper/comma separators changed to whitespace; no vectors invented:
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rpm-software-management/rpm/5dae33c3d0c51c97d5834fe2ecf768b6f5483b81/tests/rpmvercmp.at
  Original source SHA256 55df5ca66658a69b36d251f1ecef151a798baaac47d20a312ac8274718659438
  Extracted rows SHA256 4fd7a79aa7e5b4f9328ab81fccbe9b9da0c0b59b424e58b124fe1d6a140d33a1
  Commented-out known-oddity examples are not active upstream test vectors and
  were not included. Includes all active tilde/caret snapshot cases.
  RPM contributors; repository COPYING provides GPL version 2 for tests:
  https://github.com/rpm-software-management/rpm/blob/5dae33c3d0c51c97d5834fe2ecf768b6f5483b81/COPYING
  https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html
  Only input/result data retained; implementation independently follows native
  comparison semantics. No native implementation code is copied into lindm.

Adapter boundaries
------------------
  New/Fetch own HTTPS-only TLS-verified retrieval, max four redirects per each
  of at most two documents, two-minute deadline, 128MiB raw document limit
  (2MiB repomd), 512MiB decompression limit, 250000 upstream entries and 500000
  normalized package/range records. OSV individual records are bounded to 2MiB.
  Source SHA256 covers original raw compressed/ZIP bytes, not normalized JSON.
  Optional expected_sha256 is an out-of-band pin; repomd additionally binds its
  companion updateinfo by vendor SHA256. TLS is not a vendor signing-key check.
  Parse is shared online/offline. RPM_REPOMD raw imports contain updateinfo bytes;
  isolated repomd cannot be treated as an advisory document. Offline custody and
  source trust remain with the authenticated importing administrator.
  OSV JSON and single XML update nodes are always partial. A selected ZIP is
  partial. The canonical osv-vulnerabilities.storage.googleapis.com ecosystem
  all.zip URL and full updateinfo can represent complete coverage only within
  configured product/architecture and available source maps. Arbitrary mirrors
  named all.zip do not assert completeness; raw offline imports retain the
  original source configuration and its custody/pin.
  Unknown ranges, module streams, missing source mapping, unknown XML/JSON
  shapes and malformed timestamps fail explicitly; they do not produce clean.
  Rocky OSV cannot establish complete binary coverage. Red Hat/Rocky/Alma are
  not interchangeable. RHEL EUS/module products are not guessed from a major
  version. Unsupported native product formats return errors.
  Fedora adapter derives numeric releases from configuration; real captured
  fixture evidence here is Fedora44, not a claim of qualifying every release.
  Ubuntu LTS mappings are 22.04/jammy, 24.04/noble and 26.04/resolute; noble is
  the only accepted codename alias. Debian supported numeric releases are
  11/12/13; Rocky/Alma vendor major streams 8/9/10. Inventory matching
  remains exact configured release (noble/24.04 alias only), preventing silent
  minor/EUS substitution. Binary architecture aliases do not alter package EVRs.
